div.head: ECf retr 34.1b
div.ab: Que prius inuente et constitute fuerunt tempore regis Eadgari, aui sui; uerum post mortem ipsius dimisse sunt annis circiter sexaginta octo†.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 662 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page; the words in bold are the Retractator’s changes to ECf, as Liebermann prints them.

Liebermann prints the note number 16 twice in this sentence, after “fuerunt” and after “dimisse”, and there is no note 15 in this column; his note 16 (“-rant Cb Va; erant in Hv”) fits “fuerunt”, and the second 16 is probably a misprint for 18 (“d. s. fehlt Hv; dem. Cb K”, i.e. dimisse sunt), which no word in the text otherwise carries. Both are linked here to note 16 as printed, and note 18 is given as well.
Liebermann prints “†” after “octo” and gives in the outer margin of the ECf retr column the dates 975–10… (the last figures are cut off in the scan used here).

note.seg: dass dem XI. Jahrh. Eadgars Recht als Ideal galt, weiss Verf. vielleicht aus Will. Malm. Reg. II 148; er missverstand vielleicht dessen Satz III 254: Cnutone defuncto, indigenæ sibi antiquum ius uendica[bant]. Er verkennt, dass Æthelred II. und Cnut Eadgars Recht wiederholten und citirten. Ebenso 34, 3

that in the 11th century Edgar’s law counted as an ideal the author knows perhaps from Will. Malm., Reg. II 148; he perhaps misunderstood that author’s sentence III 254: Cnutone defuncto, indigenæ sibi antiquum ius uendica[bant]. He fails to recognise that Æthelred II and Cnut repeated and cited Edgar’s law. Likewise 34, 3
das Folgende aus einer unbekannten Zeittafel. Die Zahlenfehler begeht Verf. selbst (nicht etwa ein Abschreiber) laut S. 663g
what follows is from an unknown chronological table. The errors in the numbers are the author’s own (not, say, a copyist’s), according to p. 663, note g
Ed ar, dahinter Rasur Cb; Æd. stets Hv
Ed ar, followed by an erasure Cb; Æd. always Hv
d. s. fehlt Hv; dem. Cb K
d. s. lacking in Hv; dem. Cb K
an. VIII circ., am Rande LX Cb
an. VIII circ., with LX in the margin Cb

div.ab: Which had previously been devised and established in the time of King Edgar, his grandfather; but after his death they were set aside for about sixty-eight years†.
